description:
The Funeral Assistance Scheme is a welfare initiative launched by the Government of India under the aegis of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, commonly referred to as GBOCWWB.

This scheme was officially launched on 1st April 2019.

The primary objective of the Funeral Assistance Scheme is to provide financial assistance to the families of deceased construction workers.

The scheme aims to alleviate the financial burden that families face during the time of bereavement.

Under this scheme, a monetary assistance of ₹20,000 is provided to the family of the deceased construction worker.

This amount is intended to cover the expenses associated with the funeral and last rites.

The assistance is aimed at ensuring that families do not face additional financial stress during a difficult time.

To be eligible for this scheme, the applicant must be a registered construction worker under the Building and Other Construction Workers Act of 1996.

The applicant must also have contributed to the welfare fund for a minimum of one year prior to the death of the worker.

There is no specific age limit for the deceased worker under this scheme.

However, the worker must have been actively engaged in construction work at the time of their death.

The application process for the Funeral Assistance Scheme involves several steps.

First, the family of the deceased must approach the local office of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

They must submit an application form along with the required documents.

The required documents include a copy of the death certificate of the deceased worker.

Additionally, the family must provide proof of registration of the deceased worker with the welfare board.

A bank account passbook of the applicant is also required to facilitate the transfer of funds.

The application form can typically be obtained from the local welfare board office or downloaded from the official website.

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the officials of the welfare board.

The approval process usually takes about 15 to 30 days.

Upon approval, the financial assistance of ₹20,000 is disbursed directly into the bank account of the applicant.

This scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India.

The Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board operates at both the central and state levels.

Each state has its own welfare board that administers the scheme locally.

The contact details for the respective state welfare boards can be found on the official website of the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to improve the welfare of construction workers in India.

According to the Ministry of Labour and Employment, there are approximately 50 million construction workers in India.

Many of these workers are engaged in informal employment and lack social security benefits.

The Funeral Assistance Scheme aims to provide a safety net for these vulnerable workers and their families.

In addition to the Funeral Assistance Scheme, the welfare board offers various other benefits to registered workers.

These benefits include financial assistance for medical emergencies and educational support for children of construction workers.

The scheme is part of the government's commitment to enhance the living conditions of construction workers.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is tax-free.

This ensures that the full amount reaches the family without any deductions.

The scheme has been well-received by the construction worker community.

Families have reported that the assistance has significantly eased their financial burden during a time of loss.

The government has also emphasized the importance of awareness regarding the scheme.

Efforts are being made to ensure that all construction workers are aware of their rights and the benefits available to them.

Awareness campaigns are conducted at various construction sites to inform workers about the scheme.

The scheme is also aligned with the government's larger goal of providing social security to all workers in the unorganized sector.

The implementation of the scheme is monitored regularly to ensure that the benefits reach the intended beneficiaries.

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme further.

The government has set a target to increase the number of registered construction workers under the welfare board.

As of 2023, approximately 30 million workers are registered with the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The government aims to increase this number by at least 10 million by the end of 2025.

This increase is expected to enhance the reach of the Funeral Assistance Scheme and other welfare initiatives.

The scheme is also part of the larger framework of the National Policy on Labour.

This policy aims to provide comprehensive social security coverage to all workers.

The Funeral Assistance Scheme is a crucial component of this policy.

It reflects the government's commitment to improving the welfare of the most vulnerable sections of society.

In conclusion, the Funeral Assistance Scheme under the GBOCWWB provides essential financial support to the families of deceased construction workers.

With a financial assistance of ₹20,000, the scheme aims to ease the burden of funeral expenses.

The eligibility criteria ensure that only registered workers benefit from the scheme.

The application process is straightforward and designed to facilitate quick disbursement of funds.

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Labour and Employment through state welfare boards.

Efforts are ongoing to raise awareness and increase the number of registered workers.

The Funeral Assistance Scheme is a vital step towards ensuring social security for construction workers in India.
